reading: The Helicopter Museum preserves and shares the history of rotary-wing flight through a worldwide collection of more than 100 aircraft, archives, restorations and the aviation heritage of Weston-super-Mare. It is both a working heritage project and a welcoming place to visit: volunteers conserve aircraft, visiting helicopters use the airfield, and families can climb into cockpits, attend events and learn through tailored activities. Its language is precise about aircraft types, registrations, variants, engines and restoration histories, yet playful about Flying Bananas, Heli-Kids and open cockpits. What distinguishes it is the mix of rare prototypes, drones, gyroplanes, incomplete sections and familiar helicopters, each with a journey into the collection; the site treats even a nose or landing gear as a piece of a larger story.

enemies.idea: The Tandem Taker: an H-21 rear section drags itself around on two mismatched rotor wakes, hunting for a front half and temporarily attaching whatever it catches.
enemies.why: The crew can separate its improvised halves or trick the two rotors into pulling against each other.

enemies.idea: Tip-Jet Needle: a tiny Ultra-Light prototype burns bright circles around obstacles, leaving a ring that closes whenever it completes another lap.
enemies.why: Its danger is the accumulating flight path, giving players a reason to interrupt the pattern.

enemies.idea: Trial Instrument: a Wessex flight-test rig declares ordinary movement a failed performance trial and sends needles, static and calibration drones after the supposed fault.
enemies.why: Players can deliberately change their movement to make the measuring system contradict itself.

enemies.idea: Sixteen-Seat Collector: the Wessex 60 insists on filling every passenger seat with loose machinery, then sweeps the hangar for anything small enough to fit.
enemies.why: Its cargo changes its balance and exposes different routes into the cabin.

enemies.idea: Long-Nose Converter: a Whirlwind-inspired machine keeps replacing its own engine and extending its nose with stolen parts, pushing through cover as it grows.
enemies.why: Each conversion is visible and interruptible, turning its upgrade cycle into an encounter.

enemies.idea: DASH Double-Rotor: an unmanned surveillance machine uses its opposing rotors to hover motionless while it mistakes every moving shadow for a submerged target.
enemies.why: A still enemy becomes threatening through its sweeping search and its exploitable false detections.

enemies.idea: The Self-Build Cricket: a swarm-built gyrocopter makes copies from whatever spare parts are nearby; each copy inherits one conspicuous flaw from its improvised construction.
enemies.why: Observing the scavenged parts tells the crew how each copy will behave.

enemies.idea: Rotodyne Scale Flight: display models return after decades in storage and coordinate as a flock, projecting a full-sized aircraft silhouette around themselves to herd intruders.
enemies.why: The intimidating giant breaks into individually vulnerable models when its formation is disrupted.

enemies.idea: Seaspray Misreader: a roaming radar sweeps the floor for nonexistent sea traffic and labels any metal object a contact, summoning drones to investigate.
enemies.why: Loose tools and decoys can draw its attention away from the crew.

enemies.idea: The Landing-Gear Giant: the enormous XCH-62 landing gear walks without its aircraft, lowering itself over objects as if preparing for a landing that never happens.
enemies.why: A single surviving component suggests a huge absent machine and creates a moving shelter as well as a threat.

enemies.idea: Open Cockpit Host: an empty exhibit opens invitingly, then its swarm-operated controls try to recruit anyone who climbs in as the pilot of an imaginary flight.
enemies.why: A tempting shortcut becomes a cooperative rescue and a struggle over the controls.

enemies.idea: Archive Binder: technical drawings fold into gripping rotor shapes while operating manuals diagnose people as incompatible replacement parts.
enemies.why: Its attacks follow the diagrams, so reading the pages reveals the mechanism to defeat it.

enemies.idea: Approach Marshal: a landing-guidance swarm continuously moves the boundary between landing areas, treating a harmless one-metre fence as an impassable border.
enemies.why: Players can cross its shifting approach lanes at the right moment or redirect it with a convincing approach.

enemies.idea: The Spotter: a swarm telescope collects aircraft registrations and tags anything without one as an undocumented arrival to be captured for the collection.
enemies.why: Making or swapping a registration can turn a chase into a disguise puzzle.

enemies.idea: Heliliner Porter: a civilian transport cabin has become a self-directed shuttle, collecting people for a journey between exhibits that never reaches its destination.
enemies.why: The crew can board to cross a dangerous area, but must stop the endless circuit to get off.

enemies.idea: Belvedere Nose: an isolated restored nose section follows voices and tries to complete its missing aircraft with nearby scaffolding.
enemies.why: Sound draws it into assembling a body that players can rearrange against it.

enemies.idea: The Film Double: an aircraft-hire swarm dresses itself in scrap scenery and changes its behavior whenever it believes a new scene has started.
enemies.why: Crew members can manipulate its scene cues to shift it from pursuit to a harmless staged take.

enemies.idea: The Visiting-Aircraft Clerk: a hovering marshal demands confirmation of every landing, then repeatedly sends applicants back into the air while it searches for an approval.
enemies.why: A bureaucratic loop creates a timed rescue as aircraft circle and the crew finds the missing confirmation.

allies.idea: The Conservation Crew: volunteer-built repair crawlers carefully remove swarm grafts without damaging the historic components underneath.
allies.why: They offer slow, protective repairs if the crew can keep the work area clear.

allies.idea: The Activity-Pack Guide: a stubborn educational automaton teaches rotor principles using hands-on demonstrations and points out weaknesses in swarm flight patterns.
allies.why: Its lessons become practical tools, and it asks the crew to try rather than just listen.

allies.idea: The Archive Keeper: an independent cataloguing machine can identify an aircraft fragment from a drawing and find the correct manual before the swarm rewrites it.
allies.why: It turns recovered fragments into useful clues and gives players a reason to protect evidence.

allies.idea: The Access Ramp: a volunteer-maintained mobile ramp unfolds across debris and helps every member of the crew reach stranded exhibits.
allies.why: A tangible expression of the museum's accessibility opens routes for the whole party.

bosses.idea: The Curator of Everything: a hangar-sized composite of rotors, rare prototypes and exhibit fragments tries to preserve the entire collection by incorporating every visitor into it. Its protective shell opens when conflicting aircraft identities are correctly returned to their own displays.
bosses.why: The museum's breadth and care become an escalating encounter about distinguishing preservation from possession.

bosses.idea: The Endless Restoration: a workshop intelligence assembles a flying machine from sections of every unfinished project, then dismantles it again whenever the result fails to match all the manuals at once.
bosses.why: Players can redirect its repair phases and reunite compatible parts instead of simply attacking a giant machine.

bosses.idea: The Heritage Hangar Conductor: a swarm built around the local aviation collection stages every era at once, sending exhibits through overlapping takeoffs while expanding the hangar to fit its impossible timeline.
bosses.why: The crew can calm the chaos by restoring the sequence of local aviation stories, changing the arena as they go.

events.idea: A model show has become a miniature airfield: tiny Rotodynes taxi toward a full-size rotor wash, and their keeper needs a windbreak before the formation scatters.
events.why: A small rescue gives oversized rotor wash a playful, physical consequence.

events.idea: An H-21 rear section is being lifted for restoration when a swarm mistakes the lift for a departure; the crew must steady the load while its two rotor assemblies spin up.
events.why: The task is to protect a vulnerable artifact while dealing with the moving machinery around it.

events.idea: A visiting helicopter circles above the airfield because the swarm has reversed its approach guidance; someone must signal a clear route across the fence between landing areas.
events.why: The visible fence and competing signals make the rescue easy to understand and tense to execute.

events.idea: An open cockpit is filled with tiny drones rehearsing a flight; a crew member can enter to retrieve a needed switch, but the drones react to every control movement.
events.why: The cockpit is an interactive space with a reward for patience and coordination.

events.idea: A giant bubble from a Heli-Kids show drifts through the hangar carrying a trapped repair drone; rotor wash pushes it toward sharp exhibit parts.
events.why: Players must guide something fragile using the same airflow that usually causes trouble.

events.idea: A technical drawing and an operating manual disagree because the swarm has swapped pages between aircraft; matching a fragment to the right drawing reveals a safe way through a jammed mechanism.
events.why: The archive provides a solvable tactile mystery with a practical payoff.

events.idea: A single-seat Barnett gyroplane has been loaded with far too many scavenged parts for a supposed collection transfer; unload and sort them before its runaway cart reaches the airfield.
events.why: The single seat makes the absurd load clear and turns sorting into a race.

events.idea: The café's service trolley has been commandeered to deliver spare parts instead of refreshments; a warm meal and a useful component are heading to opposite destinations.
events.why: A modest choice and a moving trolley create a moment of levity between larger threats.

events.idea: A scale-model show is interrupted when swarm builders enlarge a model's missing piece using full-size hangar material; reclaim the material without crushing the models.
events.why: The difference in scales gives careful players multiple ways to solve the problem.

events.idea: Two historic aircraft components have been assigned the same exhibit arrival slot by a swarm registrar; both transport teams are converging on one narrow doorway.
events.why: A scheduling mix-up becomes a physical coordination challenge rather than a fight.

events.idea: A Wessex 60 cabin has been turned into a sixteen-seat shelter, but its twin-engine imitation keeps pulling it toward the workshop; secure it while the occupants leave.
events.why: The aircraft's passenger capacity gives the rescue a clear goal and a reason to hold position.

events.idea: A heritage hangar tour has been split across different eras by confused demonstration machines; reunite the group by matching each demonstration to its aircraft.
events.why: Local history becomes a navigation puzzle with people to help along the way.

events.idea: A Wombat gyrocopter's one-of-a-kind collection record has been attached to a pile of generic swarm parts; find the actual machine before it is sent away as a duplicate.
events.why: The tension comes from recognizing a unique exhibit among convincing lookalikes.

events.idea: An aviation film shoot's abandoned scenery is being used by swarm aircraft as landing markers; rearrange the set to lead them away from a conservation bench.
events.why: Props become an improvised airfield and allow a nonviolent diversion.
